People were walking their dogs, and I saw a group of friends. They were having a picnic. I thought, ‘I should try having a picnic next weekend.’ After some time, I decided to explore the walking trail that led to a small lake. Near the lake, I saw ducks swimming and could smell the fresh air. I sat by the lake and read a book. It was so peaceful. Later, I met a friendly jogger and he told me about a hidden garden nearby. I thought, ‘I have to visit that garden sometime.’ In the evening, I returned home feeling happy and relaxed. I realized that simple adventures like this make weekends special. I can’t wait to explore more places and create new memories.

essay: STEP UP YOUR WRITING A Mistake I Made While Traveling When I traveled to Paris for the first time, I used to carry all my important documents in one bag. I thought I would be careful enough, but I guess I wasn’t. One afternoon, I left my backpack at a café without realizing it. I must have been too distracted by the view outside the window. By the time I returned, it was gone. I wasn’t able to find it anywhere, and I started to panic. I should have double-checked before leaving the table. I could have avoided the problem if I had been more alert. I felt so frustrated and started imagining the worst—losing my passport, canceling my trip, or even going to the embassy. Thankfully, someone had returned the bag to the café staff. I was able to recover everything—my passport, money, and even my camera. After that day, I would always check my surroundings before leaving. I also used to keep everything in one place, but now I separate my valuables. I would say that mistake taught me to stay alert, especially when traveling alone. Next time, I’ll be able to handle things more calmly.

essay: STEP UP YOUR WRITING Groceries, Greetings, and Great Friendship When I first moved into this apartment complex, I didn’t know anyone. Whoever I passed in the hallway would just nod politely and walk away. One day, I accidentally dropped a bag of groceries, and someone immediately came over to help. Whatever was in her hands, she put it down without hesitation and started picking things up with me. That’s how I met Jina, a neighbor who later became one of my closest friends. She always greets whoever she sees, no matter how busy she is. Whenever she bakes, she shares a few pieces with the neighbors, including me. I can go to her place whenever I need advice—or just some good company. However different our personalities are, we always understand each other. She once told me to go with whichever decision brought me peace, and that stuck with me. Whatever the problem is, she approaches it calmly and kindly. I’ve come to believe that true friendship can start in the simplest ways. And to be honest, whoever ends up living next to her is truly lucky.

essay: STEP UP YOUR WRITING A Lucky Morning Waking up unusually refreshed, I noticed the sun shining through the curtains. Having gone to bed early the night before, I felt more energized than usual. With birds chirping outside and coffee brewing in the kitchen, the morning felt almost perfect. Heading out the door, I found that the usually crowded bus arrived right on time. Smiling at the bus driver, I grabbed a seat by the window. Spotting an empty café across from the office, I decided to treat myself to a little prework snack. Having ordered my favorite pastry, I reached into my bag—only to realize I had forgotten my wallet. Just as I started to panic, the barista smiled and said, “It’s on the house today.” Touched by the kindness, I promised to return later and pay for it. With a pastry in hand and gratitude in my heart, I arrived at work just in time for the morning meeting. Everything going smoothly, the team wrapped up early and went out for lunch together. Laughing with my coworkers, I thought, “Days like this don’t come often.” Having started the day without any expectations, I ended it feeling like the luckiest person in the world.

essay: LET’S WRITE A STORY An Unusually Eventful Day This morning started out ordinary, but my commute was full of events. I dropped my child off at school by car and then tried to park in the lot in front of the subway station, but I got into a minor collision. After dealing with the accident, I got on the train, but it was already late, and I was stuck right in the middle of rush hour. The subway was so crowded that I had to wait in line and let three trains go by before I finally got on, and I ended up arriving at the office 20 minutes late. Feeling down because of the rough start, I was surprised when a foreigner asked me for directions in English during lunch. I opened my map app and explained, “Go past the bank, then turn right at the police station, and your destination is right next to it.” He understood me well and thanked me. My colleagues praised me for speaking English fluently, and I suddenly felt proud. From a minor accident in the morning to being late for work, it wasn’t the best day. essay: LET’S WRITE A STORY A Little Chaos in Our Home This morning was completely chaotic. Around noon, I tried to hang the laundry, but heavy rain suddenly poured down, so I had to bring everything back inside. I put the wet clothes back into the spin dryer, and only then could I take a breath. In the evening, the kids tried to skip homework to watch TV, but instead we cleaned the living room and cooked dinner together. essay: LET’S WRITE A STORY My Memorable Trip to Japan Last spring, I planned a trip to Japan with my two best friends. essay: LET’S WRITE A STORY My Promise to Myself Today, I’m officially starting my diet. From now on, I’ll go jogging for about 30 minutes every morning. For breakfast, I’ll keep it light with just a boiled egg and a small vegetable salad. I ordered three months’ worth of diet meals, so I’ll stick to those only. I’ve completely cut out sugary juices and sodas, and I’ll drink only Americano without any syrup. For the next three months, I will avoid making dinner plans with friends as much as possible. On my way home from work, I will stop by the gym and commit to 40 minutes of cardio and 20 minutes of weight training. Even on weekends, I won’t eat out. To keep myself accountable and avoid giving up after just three days, I even made a deal with my parents: if I fail, I’ll give them 300,000 won each!
